newsitem.title: GERMANY: Relief on German share market after soft U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Relief on German share market after soft U.S. data.

text.p: Relief at data indicating minimal inflation pressure in the U.S. set off a strong mini-rally for German shares in post-bourse afternoon trade on Tuesday, leaving some dealers to predict more surges are ahead.

The IBIS DAX index made an enormous jump minutes after the release of lower-than-expected U.S. jobs cost data, moving into positive territory past the magic 3,000 points level to trade at 34.48 points ahead at 3,027.03 at 1421 GMT.
March DTB DAX futures were up 39.5 points at 3,044.5.
"These really were important numbers," said a Munich dealer of the report showing Q4 jobs costs rose by just 0.8 percent.

"Alan Greenspan (Federal Reserve chairman) said that if there were to be pressure on prices, it would come from labour costs. This is really good news and it's great to see a lot of the fear taken out of this market," the dealer added.
Dealers attributed the initial gains to short-covering by dealers who had bet on a bad U.S. number.
"We didn't really have real orders. Most people will sit back and assess what all this means," said a Frankfurt trader.
The Munich dealer added: "I think we will be quiet this week. We could see the DAX hitting 3,100 or even 3,150 near term but I'm not sure the market can sustain that now."
German shares had been idling all day at slightly lower levels waiting for the U.S. data and mostly shrugging off the generally positive impact of a sharply higher dollar.
After the data came out, dollar-sensitive Daimler-Benz AG built on its earlier mild gains to trade up 2.75 marks at 115.85 marks.

Engineering firm Siemens AG, also trading heavily, was up 59 pfennigs at 79.13 marks, after the market took a positive view of elements of its first quarter earnings report, despite a drop in its headline profit figure.
Even bank shares managed to pare their earlier losses.
Deutsche Bank AG was trading at 84.89 marks down just 33 pfennigs and off its intraday low of 83.25 marks.
Commerzbank AG was down 49 pfennigs at 43.20 marks, after closing bourse trade at 42.40 marks.

Commerzbank had helped trigger profit-taking on bank shares after issuing a below-forecast earnings report for 1996 in the early morning. Its profits were around 1.19 billion marks, against forecasts for 1.3 billion marks.
A report in the Financial Times recommending taking profits on German bank shares, and news that Moody's was downgrading Japanese banks, added to pressure on the sector.
Looking ahead, dealers noted that there was a raft of U.S. data due this week which could encourage investors to play safe on equities.
Tomorrow sees the release of durable goods data and jobless claims are due Thursday.
